assets._instructions: Research and document the region's natural, cultural, culinary, and craft beverage assets.

natural_anchors._instructions: Major natural features that draw visitors.
researched: 11 Finger Lakes: Canandaigua, Keuka, Seneca (deepest at 618 ft), Cayuga (longest at 40 mi), Owasco, Skaneateles, Otisco, Conesus, Hemlock, Canadice, Honeoye
Watkins Glen State Park: 19 waterfalls in a 2-mile gorge, 200-foot canyon walls
Taughannock Falls: 215-foot plunge waterfall, taller than Niagara Falls
Robert H. Treman State Park: Enfield Glen, 12 waterfalls, old-growth forest, natural swimming hole
Buttermilk Falls State Park: Cascading falls and gorge trail south of Ithaca
Letchworth State Park: Grand Canyon of the East, 3 waterfalls on the Genesee River, 550-foot cliffs, 66 miles of trails
Chimney Bluffs State Park: Eroded drumlins on Lake Ontario, surreal spire formations
Montezuma National Wildlife Refuge: 10,000-acre wetland on the Atlantic Flyway, bald eagles year-round
Grimes Glen: Devonian fossil hunting in Naples, Ontario County
Keuka Lake: Only Y-shaped lake in eastern US, Bluff Point peninsula
Finger Lakes Trail System: 580+ miles of hiking connecting the Catskills to Allegany State Park

heritage_and_culture._instructions: Historic sites, museums, notable events, Indigenous history.
researched: Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy): Finger Lakes sit at the heart of Haudenosaunee territory. Canandaigua Treaty of 1794 between the US and the Six Nations. Ganondagan State Historic Site in Victor preserves a Seneca town.
Women's Rights National Historical Park, Seneca Falls: Site of the 1848 convention. National Park Service site.
National Women's Hall of Fame, Seneca Falls: New facility in restored Seneca Knitting Mill
Harriet Tubman National Historical Park, Auburn: Tubman's home, AME Zion Church, burial site. National Park site.
Seward House Museum, Auburn: Home of Lincoln's Secretary of State
Corning Museum of Glass: 50,000+ objects spanning 3,500 years. Largest glass collection in the world.
The Rockwell Museum, Corning: Smithsonian affiliate. American art.
Glenn H. Curtiss Museum, Hammondsport: Aviation pioneer, father of naval aviation.
Mark Twain Study, Elmira College: Where Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn and Tom Sawyer.
George Eastman Museum, Rochester: World's oldest photography museum.
Strong National Museum of Play, Rochester: National Toy Hall of Fame.
Pleasant Valley Wine Company, Hammondsport: First bonded winery in the US (1860).
National Warplane Museum, Geneseo: WWII aircraft, annual airshow

culinary_identity._instructions: What food or agricultural product is this region KNOWN for nationally?
signature_products: Riesling wine: the Finger Lakes' calling card. Dry, semi-dry, and late-harvest styles. Most critically recognized Riesling region in the Americas.
Grape pie: a Naples, Ontario County tradition. Concord grape filling, September-October.
Artisan cheese: Lively Run Dairy (goat chevre), Muranda Cheese Company, Finger Lakes Cheese Trail.
Buckwheat: Penn Yan's Birkett Mills is the world's largest buckwheat processor, since 1797.
Apples and cider: Wayne County is a top apple-producing region.
All-NY ingredients cooking at the NY Wine & Culinary Center, Canandaigua
notable_producers: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery: father of vinifera winemaking in eastern US
Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard: critically acclaimed dry Riesling
Ravines Wine Cellars: Provence-trained winemaker, mineral-driven style
Lively Run Dairy: award-winning goat cheese
Ithaca Beer Co.: Flower Power IPA, regional craft beer leader
Moosewood Restaurant: defined American vegetarian cuisine since 1973
culinary_identity.culinary_reputation_nationally: The Finger Lakes is recognized nationally as the leading cool-climate wine region in the eastern US. Riesling is the signature. The farm-to-table scene is anchored by Cornell's agricultural research and a dense network of small farms. The combination of wine, cheese, and gorge landscapes gives it a distinct identity that no other eastern region matches.

wine_trails: Seneca Lake Wine Trail: ~30 members, passport program. Counties: Schuyler, Seneca, Yates, Ontario.
Cayuga Lake Wine Trail: ~15 members, passport. Oldest organized wine trail in America (est. 1983). Counties: Seneca, Cayuga, Tompkins.
Keuka Lake Wine Trail: 6 members, three digital passport options. Counties: Yates, Steuben.
Canandaigua Lake Wine Trail: ~9 members, digital passport ($60). Ontario County.
Finger Lakes Wine Country: Tourism marketing umbrella for 140+ wineries across 5 southern counties.
craft_beverage_profile.brewery_cidery_scene: Finger Lakes Beer Trail has ~50 member breweries/cideries with active passport program. Ithaca Beer Co. is the largest regional brand. Abandon Brewing in Penn Yan does acclaimed farmhouse ales. Hard cider growing from apple orchards.
craft_beverage_profile.spirits: Growing distillery scene. Notable: Finger Lakes Distilling (Burdett) produces gin, vodka, whiskey, grape brandy. No formal spirits trail.
flagship_producers: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery (Hammondsport): the pioneer, est. 1962
Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard (Dundee): dry Riesling benchmark
Ravines Wine Cellars (Geneva): mineral style, Morten Hallgren
Heron Hill Winery (Hammondsport): hilltop views, Eclipse series
Glenora Wine Cellars (Dundee): pioneer (1977), inn and restaurant
Hunt Country Vineyards (Branchport): 7th-generation farm, ice wine
Ithaca Beer Co. (Ithaca): Flower Power IPA
Keuka Brewing Company (Hammondsport): farm brewery on Keuka Lake

infrastructure._instructions: Can a visitor actually spend 2+ nights here?

flagship_properties: Belhurst Castle, Geneva: 1889 stone castle on Seneca Lake, winery, spa
Watkins Glen Harbor Hotel: lakefront, Blue Pointe Grille
Inn at Glenora Wine Cellars: vineyard lodging with Veraisons restaurant
Aurora Inn: lakeside historic inn on Cayuga Lake
Statler Hotel at Cornell, Ithaca: run by Cornell's hospitality school
lodging.gaps_or_weaknesses: Limited high-end hotel inventory outside Geneva/Watkins Glen/Ithaca. Peak season books out months ahead. Heavy reliance on vacation rentals and B&Bs.

access.bus_access: Limited. OurBus and FlixBus run NYC-Ithaca. No regular bus to other FL towns.
access.nearest_major_airport: Syracuse (SYR, 1 hr), Rochester (ROC, 30 min to Canandaigua), Elmira-Corning (ELM, local to southern FL)
access.primary_arrival_route: I-90 (NYS Thruway) east-west. I-81 north-south to Ithaca. Route 14 and Route 96A are the scenic lake roads.

visitor_centers: Finger Lakes Welcome Center, Geneva (I-90 exit)
Watkins Glen Area Chamber of Commerce
visitor_infrastructure.wayfinding_quality: Good along major lake roads. Trail signage inconsistent between individual wine trails. Digital wayfinding via trail apps and fingerlakes.org.
visitor_infrastructure.digital_presence: Strong. Finger Lakes Tourism Alliance (fingerlakes.org) is the regional hub. Individual wine trails have digital passport platforms.
visitor_infrastructure.trail_coordination_body: Finger Lakes Tourism Alliance (regional); Finger Lakes Wine Country (5 southern counties); individual trail organizations

weekend_viability._instructions: Can a visitor plan a Fri-Sun trip?
weekend_viability.reasoning: Dense wine trails, gorge hikes, and cultural anchors (Corning Museum, Seneca Falls, Ithaca) fill multiple days. The region is large, so a single weekend favors one sub-region.
weekend_viability.anchor_experience_for_overnight: Wine trail day on Seneca or Keuka Lake paired with Watkins Glen gorge. Ithaca anchors a separate weekend (gorges + food + Cornell).

uvp._instructions: What does this region have that no other NY region does?

singular_identity.statement: The Finger Lakes is the most concentrated wine-and-gorge landscape in eastern North America, with four organized wine trails, 130-plus wineries, and glacial gorges cut through 400 million years of rock.
supporting_evidence: More wine trails with passport programs than any other NY region
Cayuga Lake Wine Trail is the oldest organized wine trail in the US (1983)
Watkins Glen and Taughannock Falls are the most visited natural attractions in central NY
The Finger Lakes AVA is the largest wine-growing region east of the Rockies
Three National Park/USFWS sites (Women's Rights, Harriet Tubman, Montezuma)

destination_vs_corridor.reasoning: People drive specifically to the Finger Lakes. It sits south of I-90 and requires an intentional detour. Most visitors spend 2-4 nights.

competitive_differentiation._instructions: How is this different from neighboring regions?

vs_neighboring_regions.vs_Hudson_Valley: Hudson Valley is closer to NYC but has far less wine trail density. Finger Lakes has 4 organized wine trails with passports; Hudson Valley has one.
vs_neighboring_regions.vs_Catskills: Catskills are mountain-oriented (skiing, fly fishing). Finger Lakes are lake-and-gorge oriented (wine, waterfalls, water sports).
vs_neighboring_regions.vs_Capital_Region: Capital Region is an urban gateway. Finger Lakes is rural and spread out.
vs_neighboring_regions.vs_Central_NY: Central NY (Syracuse) is a corridor region. Finger Lakes is a destination. Overlap in Cayuga County.

unique_assets: Highest wine trail density in the eastern US
Active passport programs across wine, beer, cheese, and sweet treat trails
Corning Museum of Glass: no equivalent anywhere in NY

visitor_archetypes._instructions: Who actually comes here and why?
visitor_archetypes.primary: Mid-Atlantic wine weekenders: Couples 35-55 from NYC metro, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Toronto. Come for wine trail touring, stay 2-3 nights, base near Seneca or Keuka Lake, visit 4-8 wineries per trip.
visitor_archetypes.secondary: Regional family hikers: Families from Rochester, Syracuse, Buffalo. Come for gorge hikes, lake swimming, camping. Summer-concentrated, repeat visitors.
visitor_archetypes.emerging: Serious wine pilgrims: Sommeliers, wine writers, wine-educated travelers who come for dry Riesling. Smaller in number but high influence. Visit in shoulder season.

rtn_partnership_pitch._instructions: What would you say to a DMO to get them to join?
rtn_partnership_pitch.key_message: The Finger Lakes has the most developed trail infrastructure in Upstate NY. Joining Upstate connects isolated wine trails to a statewide 75-trail discovery platform. For gap counties (Livingston, Monroe, Wayne), Upstate provides the framework to launch new trails.
gaps_we_solve: Cross-trail discovery: Seneca Lake visitors don't know about the Cheese Trail unless someone connects them
Gap county trail activation with proven playbook
rtn_partnership_pitch.comparable_success: Lake Erie Wine Country saw increased passport sales after joining a regional tourism network. The same model across Finger Lakes' 12 trails would be transformative.

seasonality._instructions: When should visitors come, and for what?

peak_season.crowd_level: High. Watkins Glen State Park hits capacity by 10am on summer Saturdays. Lodging books months ahead.
peak_season.pricing_pressure: Moderate-high. Lakefront properties charge 40-60% premiums. Airbnb spikes on race and festival weekends.

shoulder_season.opportunity: The Finger Lakes in late May and June is the region's best-kept timing secret. Gorges run high from snowmelt. Vineyards in full leaf but tasting rooms uncrowded. Prices 20-30% below summer.
what_makes_it_worth_it: Gorge waterfalls at peak flow from spring runoff
Wine tasting rooms with no lines
Cornell Botanic Gardens peak bloom in May-June
Ithaca Farmers Market opens for the season
Late October: harvest wine events, off-peak pricing
shoulder_season.under_visited_reason: Perception that wine country is a fall thing. Most visitors default to September-October.

anchors: Ice wine events on Keuka Lake (February-March)
Holiday shopping in Gaffer District, Corning
off_season.viable: Partially. Wine trails reduce hours. Most gorge trails close for ice safety. Depends on indoor cultural anchors.

signature_events._instructions: Named annual events that anchor visits.

events.name: Finger Lakes Wine Festival
events.draw: Largest wine festival in the eastern US. 80+ wineries.

events.name: NASCAR Cup Series at Watkins Glen
Naples Grape Festival
events.draw: Grape pies, wine, arts. A tradition since 1961.

events.name: GlassFest
events.draw: Street festival celebrating glass art in the Gaffer District.

events.name: Ithaca Festival
events.draw: Arts, music, and food. Showcases Ithaca's creative community.

seasonal_guide_headline._instructions: One line per season for an editorial callout.
seasonal_guide_headline.spring: The gorges run loud and the tasting rooms run quiet — come before everyone else remembers.
seasonal_guide_headline.summer: Lake days, gorge walks, and wine flights that stretch past sunset on a porch above Seneca.
seasonal_guide_headline.fall: Harvest is the main event — the vines turn gold, the Riesling comes in, and the whole region smells like Concord grapes.
seasonal_guide_headline.winter: The lakes don't freeze, the ice wine does — and Corning's glass furnaces keep the Gaffer District warm year-round.

county_trail_map._instructions: For each county, list active trails. Flag gaps.

Livingston.gap_opportunity: Letchworth State Park anchor. Potential Genesee Valley Outdoor Trail linking Letchworth, Conesus Lake, and Geneseo farms.

Monroe.gap_opportunity: Rochester has 20+ breweries, Eastman Museum, Strong Museum, Public Market. Rochester Cultural Trail or Craft Beverage Trail is the play.

Wayne.gap_opportunity: Lake Ontario shoreline, top apple county, Erie Canal heritage, Chimney Bluffs. Potential agritourism or heritage trail.

guide_framing._instructions: Quick notes for the Phase 4 guide writer.
guide_framing.emotional_hook: The light on the water. Every Finger Lake reflects the sky differently. The gorges amplify sound — you hear a waterfall before you see it. The tasting rooms smell like wet stone and cold fruit. This region registers through all the senses before you have opened a trail map.
guide_framing.lede_angle: Open with the feeling of arriving — the descent into the lake basin, the moment the land drops away and water appears. Not the wine statistics. Let the reader feel the geography first, earn the wine story second.
what_to_avoid: Don't lead with winery counts — that's a brochure stat, not a feeling
Don't treat the region as one place — it's multiple sub-destinations
Don't ignore the gorges in favor of wine
Don't use any forbidden Upstate phrases
guide_framing.comparable_editorial_tone: Willamette Valley coverage in Bon Appetit — specific about producers, honest about what's developing, respects the reader's intelligence.
